title: POC scoping - workload modeling (Aurora Pay)
summary: Discovery / POC scoping for Aurora Pay focusing on workload characterization (QPS, concurrency, token distributions), success criteria and benchmark plan. Customer wants predictable latency under peak traffic, PCI/PII-safe deployment (VPC/private), and cost estimates for a dedicated pool. Next steps: Redwood to run benchmark with synthetic trace, customer to share sample traffic and token histograms, schedule perf run and security doc handoff.
topics: deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
action_items: Ben Ortiz: run initial benchmark with synthetic trace + 3 sessions of token distributions - due 2027-11-27
Karen Malik: export 7 days of anonymized request logs and sample prompts for token histogram - due 2027-11-24
Alice Chen: send dedicated capacity pricing and pilot SOW - due 2027-11-23
Ravi Patel: confirm VPC peering window and provide networking contacts - due 2027-11-25
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-tier benchmark (baseline + 3x peak) and share results
Customer to send sample payloads and histogram CSV
Schedule 1-hour perf-run (SE-led) next week to validate P95/P99

Follow-up to include cost per 1M tokens for baseline and peak profiles
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-20
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Karen Malik (Aurora Pay - Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Aurora Pay - SRE), Sophia Li (Product), Marcus Dunn (Security), Lina Gomez (Data Eng)

Auto-summary: Quick discovery to nail down POC success criteria, traffic model, and benchmark plan. Customer emphasizes PCI constraints and the need for predictable latency during spikes. Redwood proposes dedicated pool + workload-specific batching/quantization recommendations.

00:00 Alice Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll keep this pretty structured — goal is to scope the poc and get concrete numbers for workload modeling. ben will cover the perf questions; i'll handle process and pricing notes.
00:12 Karen Malik: thanks Alice. we want to be explicit around success criteria — for us that's latency under load, consistent token quality, and of course we need the infra to meet PCI and our auditors.
00:22 Ben Ortiz: great, can you give us a quick picture of current traffic? qps, typical payload sizes, and where the spikes happen.
00:30 Karen Malik: yeah so baseline is about 95 qps across our api that calls the model for things like classification + enrichment. typical prompt size is small, avg input tokens ~ 35-45, output tokens around 80-140 depending on flow. spikes: during merchant checkout peaks up to ~1,200 qps for short windows, about 5-7 minutes; daily peak around 600 qps at noon.
01:05 Ben Ortiz: got it — 95 baseline, short spike to 1.2k. what's concurrency look like? active sessions?
01:12 Ravi Patel: concurrency on the client side is a bit fuzzy, but our gateway sees ~300 concurrent connections during baseline and up to ~3,200 during biggest spikes because each request is quick. the model calls are sync — we wait for the model response before returning.
01:30 Ben Ortiz: ok that maps. for modeling we usually look at qps, concurrent inferences, and avg tokens per inference — which you gave. do you have token distribution histograms? percentiles?
01:42 Lina Gomez: we can export a histogram, right now rough p50 input tokens 40, p95 120 (that's heavy flow for refunds), output p50 110, p95 320 — the long outputs are rarer. i'll pull exact CSV.
02:00 Ben Ortiz: perfect, that will let us build a realistic synthetic trace. for the poc what are your latency SLOs? p95/p99?
02:08 Karen Malik: p95 under 300 ms would be ideal for the short prompts. for longer outputs we can accept up to 800 ms p95. p99 we'd like under 2s if possible. cost is secondary but we need ballpark unit economics.
02:28 Ben Ortiz: pushing 300ms p95 at 1.2k qps is non-trivial but doable with dedicated infra + batching and KV cache for prefixes. we should run a benchmark with your token hist to see where we land.
02:40 Sophia Li: just to add, we need to keep output quality the same — we can't have regression vs current model. so evaluation & quality pass/fail criterion should be included.
02:52 Alice Chen: good point, include a small eval set in the sample prompts so we measure quality drift.
03:00 Marcus Dunn: on security — PCI is mandatory; we need VPC, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), audit logs, and SSO/SAML. are those available in dedicated/private?
03:12 Ben Ortiz: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and audit logs. Dedicated pools can be configured in a VPC with our private control plane. we'll attach the security pack.
03:25 Marcus Dunn: and data retention? we need zero retention of PII and an option to disable telemetry.
03:32 Alice Chen: we can toggle retention for the POC — zero retention option is available on Private and Dedicated with the right config. we'll document that in the security pack.
03:45 Karen Malik: timeline — we'd like to have a short 4-week pilot, proof within two weeks to decide. is that realistic?
03:52 Ben Ortiz: timeline is tight but workable. week 0: share artifacts + sample data, week 1: bench runs and tuning, week 2: higher-fidelity perf run and quality eval, week 3-4: pilot run in dedicated pool and handoff. so yes, 4 weeks for a meaningful pilot.
04:15 Alice Chen: for the bench runs we need a couple of configurations to compare: hosted baseline (what you'd get out of box), dedicated reserved pool with 2-4 GPU nodes depending on model, and a private VPC variant. that will give cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:33 Ben Ortiz: what model are you running today?
04:36 Karen Malik: currently using an open model (we call it 'Aurora-small' internally) for most flows; for critical flows we sometimes fallback to a larger commercial model. ideally we want Redwood to serve our open weights with quantization.
04:52 Ben Ortiz: that matches our onboarding path. we'll test with a quantized 8-bit variant and one fp16 variant for quality delta.
04:58 Sophia Li: can Redwood simulate the traffic pattern — daily baseline + short large spike? we want to know how steady-state batching reacts to spikes.
05:06 Ben Ortiz: yes, synthetic trace generation is standard. if you provide the histogram + request timestamps sample we can replay exact spike shapes.
05:15 Karen Malik: i'll have the team export the last 7 days of logs and a sample of prompts. lina will send that.
05:22 Lina Gomez: noted — i'll sanitize PII and produce histograms and sample prompts by end of day thursday.
05:30 Ben Ortiz: for metrics, we'll capture tokens/sec, GPU utilization, end-to-end latency (including network), and cost per 1M tokens. we'll also produce a recommended batch size and cache hit rates.
05:45 Ravi Patel: for networking, we need to know requirements for VPC peering and egress IPs. our change window is next Tuesday.
05:52 Alice Chen: we'll send network reqs and a proposed peering window. Ben — can you include the peering port ranges?
05:58 Ben Ortiz: yes, i'll include port ranges and expected throughput.
06:05 Karen Malik: quality gating — we want a pass/fail on: 1) semantic parity on core flows (<2% regression on BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics we track), 2) latency SLOs hit, 3) cost under target (we'll give target later).
06:25 Ben Ortiz: makes sense. we'll run automatic evals on the sample set and flag regressions.
06:32 Sophia Li: what about autoscaling — we don't want cold-starts during spikes to blow latency.
06:38 Ben Ortiz: dedicated pools can keep a warm pool and autoscale more conservatively for spikes; there is also fast-fallback to a lower-cost region but for PCI that may not be allowed.
06:50 Marcus Dunn: fallback across regions is prohibited for us. must be within EU/US regions only.
06:55 Alice Chen: we'll mark region constraints in the SOW.
07:00 Ben Ortiz: one more technical question — do you use many long-context sessions (documents, user history) that increase token counts?
07:08 Karen Malik: yes, for refunds and anti-fraud checks we sometimes stitch 2-3 previous messages; that pushes input tokens to p95 ~120-200 occasionally.
07:20 Ben Ortiz: ok we'll include a long-context case in the benchmark to see memory/KV cache effects.
07:28 Alice Chen: recapping next steps: ben runs initial bench with synthetic baseline + 3x spike; karen/lina send logs and sample prompts; alice sends pricing and security pack; rafi (ravi) gives networking window. any other asks?
07:45 Ravi Patel: please include expected cost delta between quantized 8-bit and fp16 options.
07:50 Ben Ortiz: will do.
07:55 Sophia Li: schedule a 1-hour perf validation next wed?
08:00 Alice Chen: sounds good, I'll propose time. thanks everyone.

End notes: rough run-time timestamps may drift slightly; some speaker labels were automated and may not map perfectly. References shared: link to Redwood security pack (link sent after call), synthetic-trace-template.csv (will be provided), dedicated-capacity-SOW-draft.pdf (to follow).
